methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's cancellation of four NoVA data centers signals political and community resistance to AI infrastructure even in Virginia's most concentrated tech hub, potentially stalling the physical substrate needed for either deep or distributed AI capability development across the Commonwealth.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents intentional capability-building outside traditional tech corridors, targeting leadership development that could enable peer-to-peer AI fluency networks beyond NoVA if successfully scaled and replicated regionally.

signals.title: Military spouse uses AI to help veterans navigate VA benefits - DC Military
signals.signal_reading: A military spouse creating AI tools for veterans demonstrates grassroots, mission-driven AI development by non-traditional actors—exactly the distributed, deep problem-solving capacity that characterizes bottom-up capability building rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke coalition hiring external consultants to study an AI center plan suggests aspiration for concentrated capability outside NoVA, but reliance on Texas expertise rather than indigenous capacity signals potential dependence patterns that may reinforce rather than redistribute concentration.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's statewide AI cybersecurity directive centralizes preparedness planning at the state level, potentially creating deep capability nodes in Richmond government agencies while leaving distribution of actual implementation capacity across regions uncertain.
